about: The colour scales of the map viewer's raster layers, defined only here. scripts/data_layers.py colours the overlay images with them and copies them into each site's manifest, from which the viewer draws its legends, so a legend shows the colours of its map. A scale of stops spreads them evenly over the layer's domain (the domain stays in the site's manifest) and interpolates between them in OKLab, as the legend's colour bar does; a scale of classes gives one colour to each class, in increasing order. They are the colours of the poster's maps: matplotlib's viridis for the elevation, and ColorBrewer schemes for the others (this product includes color specifications and designs developed by Cynthia Brewer, http://colorbrewer.org/).

elevation.reads: dark purple is low ground, yellow high ground

sigma.scheme: ColorBrewer Purples, 9 classes, without the near-white first one
sigma.reads: light is a sharp dry-to-wet transition, dark an uncertain one

emersion.reads: light is mostly under water, dark mostly out of it

delay.scheme: ColorBrewer Oranges without its lightest 15 %, 9 stops
delay.reads: light is no delay, dark the longest
